name: Thikarisuchus
isnote: English Wikipedia places it in the neosuchian family Wannchampsidae; the atlas has no clade for that family, so it sits in Neosuchia (the backbone had it in Pholidosauridae, which the source does not support).
sum: Thikarisuchus is a small heterodont neosuchian from the Cenomanian Blackleaf Formation of Montana, known from a juvenile skull and partial skeleton.
wsnote: The holotype skull is about 5.5 cm long and the animal was immature; a referred dentary suggests an individual about twice that size. No body length is given.
holotype: MOR 11969 (nicknamed 'Elton'), most of a skull plus partial postcranial remains, found in 2021 in the Vaughn Member of the Blackleaf Formation near Lima, southwest Montana.
material: The holotype and a referred dentary fragment (MOR 11969-3).
biology: The description concerns the paleoecology of heterodont neosuchians; the sources consulted here give no more on its diet.
author: Allen et al. 2025

sources.text: Allen, H. J., Wilberg, E. W., Turner, A. H. and Varricchio, D. J. 2025. A new, diminutive, heterodont neosuchian from the Blackleaf Formation's Vaughn Member (Cenomanian) of southwest Montana, with implications for heterodont neosuchian paleoecology. Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, e2542185.

dates_note: No PBDB occurrences. Age is the Cenomanian stage of the ICS chart, as named in the description.
